subject: Dedicated capacity ask: Paladin AI — US/EU/APAC pool alignment
messages:
From: Mike Chen <mike.chen@paladin.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Park <alex.park@paladin.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool ask: Paladin AI (US/EU/APAC)

Sean —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Paladin is moving fast on a pilot that will be live with select customers in Q4, and we need to lock in dedicated capacity sizing and pricing to finish our procurement runway. High level:

- Region coverage: US (primary), EU (GDPR customers), APAC (beta customers in SG/HK)
- Expected steady-state QPS: ~1200 requests/minute globally (rough distribution: 60% US, 30% EU, 10% APAC)
- Burst profile: up to 3x steady-state for black-friday / product launches (short spikes, ~5–10 minute windows)
- Sequence lengths: median 256 tokens; 95th percentile ~1024 tokens
- Requirement: model family tbd but want to reserve capacity for a 13B-ish open model quantized profile; need predictable throughput and failover across regions.

Can you share a suggested pool sizing (gpus per region), estimated monthly committed units, and a draft SOW your team would need to move forward? Procurement wants a draft SOW + pricing before the end of next week.

Thanks —
Mike Chen
Head of Platform
Paladin AI

Attachment: Paladin_traffic_profile_Q2-2027.csv (csv)

Mike —

Appreciate the clear brief. We'll put together a region-by-region sizing recommendation and a sketch SOW for procurement. Initial plan:

1) Quick follow-up call to validate traffic profile assumptions (30m).
2) Preliminary sizing: propose a conservative reserve + 20% burst buffer while we ramp (numbers below are placeholder until we see the CSV).
3) Draft SOW and cost estimate for review.

Can we do a call Monday morning PT? If you prefer, Karthik/ I can start with a back-of-envelope and circulate before the call.

Sean Gallagher

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 26 Jun 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Dedicated pool ask — preliminary regional sizing (draft)

Sean / team —

I sketched an initial sizing plan based on Mike's estimates (steady-state 1200 rpm, burst up to 3x, median seq 256, p95 1024). This is a quick draft; we should validate with the CSV before locking numbers. Key assumptions noted inline.

Proposal (GPU-equivalent slots; assume 90% utilization target for steady-state):
- US (60% traffic): 18 slots steady-state + 6 surge = 24 slots total (equivalent to ~8 x A100-40GB or 12 x H100-q configurations depending on quantization).
- EU (30%): 9 slots steady + 3 surge = 12 slots total.
- APAC (10%): 3 slots steady + 2 surge = 5 slots total (start small; can route to US in low-latency fallback).

Tradeoffs / notes:
- If Paladin adopts a heavier model (30B), swap factor ~2.2x GPU needs — budget that risk in the SOW.
- Burst buffer is costly if we reserve 100% committed; recommend a hybrid: committed baseline + burstable reserved pool (monthly commit + burst credits).
- Sequence length distribution matters: p95 1024 impacts memory and kv-cache; recommend we request the CSV profile broken out by request type.

Next actions:
- Ask Paladin for per-endpoint token distribution and hourly QPS for a 24h sample.
- Draft SOW with a 90-day ramp, trial credits for first month, and a 6–12 month commit window with an option to scale.

I'll draft the attached capacity_estimate_breakdown.xlsx and a short note for procurement.

Karthik
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachment: capacity_estimate_breakdown.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 10:46:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Dedicated pool ask — technical clarifications

Team / Sean —

A couple of things I need from Paladin to refine the sizing and kernel choices: 

1) Endpoint breakdown: which endpoints are chat vs. embed vs. bulk inference? Chat-style workloads have higher kv-cache retention and different batching efficiency.
2) Typical prompt and response token split (we need input vs. output avg).
3) Desired availability SLAs per region (99.9 vs 99.95 impacts standby capacity).
4) Are they sensitive to cold-start latency for model swaps?

If Paladin can share the Paladin_traffic_profile_Q2-2027.csv (hourly) and a sample request set (anonymized), I can run a quick simulation and update the slot counts.

Irene Choi
Infrastructure PM, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated pool ask: Procurement questions + SOW request

Hello Sean —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A few procurement items to confirm before we take the SOW to legal: 

- Contract term: Paladin prefers a 12-month committed term with quarterly usage reconciliation. Are you able to offer a ramp schedule tied to monthly commit increases?
- Credits: We request 1 month trial credits for the first 30 days; can those be applied against committed spend?
- Data residency: For EU traffic, we need assurance that logs/metrics stay in-region and SOC-2 audit evidence.
- Pricing: Please provide a straightforward committed vs burst pricing table in the SOW.

Also attach whatever SOW draft you have; procurement will annotate.

Thanks —
Paladin Procurement Team

Attachment: procurement_questions.txt (txt)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool ask: Paladin AI — US/EU/APAC pool alignment

Mike / Procurement —

Thanks — attaching an initial SOW (SOW_Paladin_v0.3.pdf) and the capacity workbook. Short answers inline: 

- Term: 12 months commit with a 90-day ramp schedule included. We can add monthly commit increase windows (section 2.1).
- Trial credits: we can provide a one-month credit applied to month 1 committed spend (not to burst credits) — we'll note that explicitly in the SOW.
- Data residency: Redwood Private control plane + region-local logs for EU traffic; I'll pull SOC2 evidence links for legal.
- Pricing: attached table with committed vs burst rates and an illustration (see capacity_estimate_breakdown.xlsx).

Karthik's preliminary regional slots are conservative; Irene will run the simulation once we get the CSV Mike attached earlier. Proposed next steps:

1) Quick call to validate CSV assumptions (Mon 10am PT?)
2) Irene runs simulation and updates slot counts + SOW appendix
3) Procurement sends annotated SOW back; legal loop if needed.

I'm OK approving the temporary three-week buffer (month 1 surge credits) to unblock procurement — Marissa, Hannah, can you confirm operational alignment for a soft cap in APAC (route to US fallback) and EU log residency? If yes, I'll mark this as approved from sales side and push SOW to DocuSign after procurement review.

Thanks —
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOW_Paladin_v0.3.pdf (pdf); capacity_estimate_breakdown.xlsx (xlsx)
